image_description: A low-angle shot of a large pipe organ installed in a church or concert hall balcony. The image features a prominent central section with vertical silver pipes of varying heights, flanked by ornate wooden casework with carved details. Above the main console area, there is a secondary tier of pipes arranged in a fan-like or angled structure against a white vaulted ceiling. The lighting is warm, highlighting the wood textures and metallic sheen of the pipes.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific classification of the instrument as a pipe organ and distinguish it from other architectural structures.
To verify the 3D structural integrity of the pipes and ensure they are properly grounded in the casing without melting or floating artifacts.
To check for boundary bleeding between the individual pipes and the background/casing, ensuring distinct separation.
To assess general image quality, texture consistency, and detect any subtle generative distortions in the wood grain or metal reflections.

focus_areas: Symmetry and alignment of vertical pipes
Texture consistency of wooden casework vs. metallic pipes
Structural plausibility of the upper pipe tier
Edge sharpness between pipes and background
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the upper tier of pipes; AI often struggles with complex, non-standard geometric arrangements like the angled/fan-shaped pipes seen here. Verify if the connections to the wall/ceiling look physically plausible or if they 'melt' into the architecture. Check for repetitive texture patterns in the wood that might indicate generative artifacts.
